part.text: {"answer_notes":{},"claims":[{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q106C","quote":"Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?"}],"id":"O-C1","items":["Q106C"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q106C records the interviewer's own binary report of whether the interviewer was approached by community and/or political party representatives in connection with the interview setting; the referent is the interviewer's experience, not the respondent's exposure or any campaign activity. Codes 0 = No and 1 = Yes exhaust the substantive field; there is no refused/don't-know layer, so a 0 asserts absence of approach, not a missing value."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q106D","quote":"Did you feel threatened during the interview?"},{"field":"Q106E","quote":"Were you physically threatened during the interview?"}],"id":"O-C2","items":["Q106D","Q106E"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q106D and Q106E are interviewer-report, interview-time fields about felt threat (Q106D) and physical threat (Q106E); they are distinct acts, not a severity scale: yes on Q106E does not entail yes on Q106D and vice versa. Both are binary 0 = No / 1 = Yes with no special codes, so 0 records absence of the threat experience during the interview, not withheld answer."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q109F","quote":"What was the respondent's attitude toward you during the interview? Was he or she: honest, in between, or misleading?"}],"id":"O-C3","items":["Q109F"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q109F is a three-point interviewer judgment about the respondent's perceived honesty during the interview (1 = Honest | 2 = In between | 3 = Misleading). Its grain is the interview, its source is interviewer assessment, and it is one member of a same-stem attitude battery; it records an evaluative impression, not a verified fact about respondent truthfulness, and 'in between' is a substantive middle state rather than missing."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q28","quote":"The [president] must always obey the laws and the courts, even if [he] thinks they are wrong."}],"id":"O-C4","items":["Q28"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q28 is a forced-choice item where the respondent endorses one of two named statements, scaled 1–4 by strength plus 5 = Agree with neither; the endorsed side identifies a view about presidential boundness by law and courts. Refused and don't know are separate special codes, so 5 = Agree with neither is a positive substantive non-alignment act, not a missing response."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q29B","quote":"It is legitimate for the armed forces to take control of government when elected leaders abuse power for their own ends."}],"id":"O-C5","items":["Q29B"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q29B parallels Q28's structure but its two statements concern military intervention in the political process versus a conditional legitimacy of armed-forces takeover; the same 1–5 substantive coding applies with identical honor for 'neither'. Q28 and Q29B are separate attitudinal acts about different referents (presidential law-obedience vs. military takeover conditions) and must not be collapsed as one constitutionalism score."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q48A","quote":"Who should be responsible for: making sure that, once elected, [members of Parliament] do their jobs?"}],"id":"O-C6","items":["Q48A"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q48A is a single-choice attribution item naming who should be accountable for elected MPs' performance; options include The President / Executive, The Parliament / local government council, Their Political Party, The Voters, No One. The referent is a normative allocation of accountability, not a report of observed practice; option 4 = No One is a positive substantive stance distinct from refused/don't know."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q48A","quote":"The Parliament / local government council"},{"field":"Q48B","quote":"Who should be responsible for: making sure that, once elected, the [president] does [his] job?"}],"id":"O-C7","items":["Q48A","Q48B"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q48A and Q48B form a matched pair on the same normative dimension, differing only in the object whose performance must be ensured (MPs vs. president); their option sets share codes 0–4 but Q48B lacks a separate local-government marker, so the pair is comparable at the option-family level, not necessarily at the code-label level."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q50B","quote":"she will be criticized, called names, or harassed by others in the community?"},{"field":"Q53C","quote":"she will be criticized, harassed, or shamed by others in the community?"}],"id":"O-C8","items":["Q50B","Q53C"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q50B (anticipated harassment if a woman runs for office) and Q53C (anticipated shaming if a woman reports gender-based violence) share a four-point likelihood coding (1 = Very unlikely to 4 = Very likely) but ask about different scenarios and different triggering acts, so they cannot be pooled as one harassment measure; each is conditional on a hypothetical woman in the respondent's community, a stance, not a report of an actual event."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q51A","quote":"should government and elected officials be doing more than they are doing now to advance the rights and equality of women"}],"id":"O-C9","items":["Q51A"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q51A uses a five-point amount scale whose endpoints reverse activity direction (1 = Much less to 5 = Much more), with 3 = About the right amount as a middle substantive state; 0 is not valid here, distinguishing it from binary and four-point items in the same selected set. Response act is a normative demand judgment about government effort on women's equality."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q51B","quote":"which of the following issues related to women's rights and equality do you think is the most important"}],"id":"O-C10","items":["Q51B"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q51B is a single-choice issue–priority item with a substantive 0 = None of these / There are no issues for government to address and codes 1–6 naming issue domains; the question asks for the most important issue, so a selected code records singular prioritization, not salience ranking or issue attitudes. Refused/don't know remain special, distinct from the 0 no-issue stance."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q63B","quote":"using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates"}],"id":"O-C11","items":["Q63B"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q63B is a conditional agree/disagree item about justifiability of a specific pandemic measure; its routing shows a distinct 97 = Not applicable (COV1=0, 8 or 9) code, so its denominator is limited to COVID-heard/asked respondents. It measures approval of one named measure, not a general liberty–security tradeoff, and neither agrees side nor item can be read as actual government conduct."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q97","quote":"Who do you think sent us to do this interview?"}],"id":"O-C12","items":["Q97"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q97 is a thirteen-option attribution item where the respondent names who they believe commissioned the interview; codes include 0 = No one, 1 = 'Afrobarometer' or national partner, 8 = Government, 9 = International organization, 10 = God, 95 = Other. The act registers the respondent's belief about sponsorship and cannot be treated as respondent identity or as a factual report about the survey operator."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q98A","quote":"Willing to participate in follow-up surveys"}],"id":"O-C13","items":["Q98A"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q98A records consent to be re-contacted for follow-up surveys as a binary 0 = No / 1 = Yes, with a distinct 7 = Not applicable [Respondent does not have a mobile phone number]; that code is a structural non-eligibility, not a refusal, so the field's denominator is respondents with a contactable mobile context. It is a stated willingness, not evidence of actual follow-up."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q97","quote":"Political party or politician"},{"field":"Q106C","quote":"community and/or political party representatives"}],"id":"O-C14","items":["Q97","Q106C"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q97 and Q106C both register political-party-related interviewer/respondent context but at different grains and acts: Q97 asks the respondent for a belief about who sponsored the survey (party as a possible sponsor), while Q106C asks the interviewer whether representatives approached the interview. Response to Q97 cannot substitute for Q106C and neither entails the other."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q106D","quote":"Did you feel threatened during the interview?","},{"field":"Q109F","quote":"1 = Honest | 2 = In between | 3 = Misleading"}],"id":"O-C15","items":["Q106D","Q109F"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q106D and Q109F are both interviewer-report interview-quality fields but differ in act and scale: Q106D is a binary yes/no experience question with no special codes, while Q109F is a three-category evaluative judgment;
